claims.text: The new framework will predict total thermal conductivity with an average error below 20%.
The below-20% average error will apply over 200–1200 K to near-equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr containing up to 1 wt.% oxygen.
Earlier treatments merge lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions.
Earlier treatments frequently deviate from experimental data by at least 30%.
The intended material is single-phase, near-equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr with up to 1 wt.% oxygen and minimal porosity or second-phase inclusions.
The proposed approach combines first-principles phonon and electron transport calculations with data-driven corrections for chemical disorder and minor oxygen effects.
Local chemical-environment fluctuations and oxygen defect sites modulate phonon scattering.
Local chemical-environment fluctuations and oxygen defect sites affect electron transport.
Computed dispersion relations, density of states, and scattering rates enable the model to decouple lattice and electronic thermal transport.
Separately treating lattice and electronic transport enables better tracking of each contribution's temperature dependence.
The framework resolves effects of multielement disorder and defect interactions that simpler approaches do not fully capture.
Predicted total thermal conductivity will be within 10–20% of measurements.
Lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions are comparable below 200 K.
Electronic conduction predominates above 300 K.
Earlier methods do not fully account for local topological disorder.
Earlier methods often rely on a single global Debye temperature.
The proposed accuracy is limited to single-phase HfNbTaTiZr with no more than 1 wt.% oxygen and minimal second-phase formation.
Accuracy above 1 wt.% oxygen or under severe compositional gradients is unverified.
Local compositional fluctuations and extrinsic defects may introduce additional scattering channels at higher doping levels or in multiphase material.
An average prediction error above 20%, or failure to reproduce the temperature dependence and transport crossover, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The principal accuracy claim is limited to 200–1200 K, but the predicted crossover is stated to occur below 200 K and the falsification experiment extends to 100 K. Thus, crossover behavior outside the stated applicability range is nevertheless made part of the decisive test.
